solutionMethods.explanation: Align the place values of \(1011\) and \(0110\). In binary, a column total of \(2\) is written as \(0\), with \(1\) carried to the next place. From right to left, the ones column gives \(1\), and each of the next three columns totals \(2\) after accounting for carries. Thus the sum is \(10001\) in binary, whose nonzero places have decimal values \(16\) and \(1\). The decimal sum is \(16+1=17\).

reference.question: Add the binary numbers 1011 and 110. What is their sum in decimal?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Convert before adding

\(1011\text{ (binary)}=11\) and \(110\text{ (binary)}=6\), so their sum is 17.

Method 2: Add in binary first

Align the place values of \(1011\) and \(0110\). In binary, a column total of \(2\) is written as \(0\), with \(1\) carried to the next place. From right to left, the ones column gives \(1\), and each of the next three columns totals \(2\) after accounting for carries. Thus the sum is \(10001\) in binary, whose nonzero places have decimal values \(16\) and \(1\). The decimal sum is \(16+1=17\).
